newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania court clears Iliescu's poll bid.
newsitem.headline: Romania court clears Iliescu's poll bid.

text.p: Romania's constitutional court has cleared President Ion Iliescu's path to re-election by rejecting challenges that his candidacy was breaking post-communist laws, a court magistrate said on Monday.
The ruling was announced after a secretive weekend sitting by the nine-member court.
Challengers had argued that Iliescu, in power since the 1989 fall of communism, was breaching the 1991 constitution by bidding to stay in office.

The court deemed that Iliescu, who won elections in 1990 and 1992, was not breaking the legal limit of two four-year terms in office since his first ballot triumph pre-dated the post-communist constitution.
Iliescu is favourite to win the presidential polls on November 3, which coincide with parliamentary elections.

"His (Iliescu's) 1990-1992 mandate was not the same as his present mandate," court magistrate Gheorghe Iancu said. The constitution adopted in 1991 gives the president considerable powers and makes Romania a semi-presidential republic.

The court rejected 67 challenges lodged last week by contesters including Romania's best-known communist-era dissident, Doina Cornea, the League for Human Rights (LADO) and the Civic Alliance, a small centrist political group.
Cornea has long accused Iliescu, a former communist functionary, of abuse of power and betraying the revolution.

The court is expected to rule later this week on another 11 challenges against Iliescu's bid which were submitted over the weekend, Iancu said. "They may still contain arguments that might lead to a contrary ruling," he added.
LADO chairman Niculae Draganesti, a lawyer, said he had been denied the right to be present in court.
LADO would ask that the court, three of whose judges were appointed by Iliescu, should be revoked. "This is not Romania's constitutional court, it's Iliescu's court," said Draganesti.
